messages.author: e7dd1afd04d0accc
messages.subject: Interactions in QTLs
parts:
Hi Karl,

I am kinda confused with how to deal with interactions in QTLs. I tried the following to determine which pairs of QTLs are interacting and I got several significant interactions based on the p-values.

addint(data, qtl=qtl, method="hk")

However, when I try to fit the interactions using fitqtl, e.g. a simple case where model=y~Q1+Q2+Q1:Q2, I get weird results where PVE summed across all Q1, Q2, Q1:Q2 is higher than PVE given by the model.

Following that, when I try to do refineqtl with the same model, the LOD scores for the QTL and remaining region in the chromosome goes up too. When I looked at the plot from plotLodProfile, it appears that there is an additional QTL on the same chromosome based on the same 0.05% LOD cutoff (I think that is not real).

Is it right to fit interactions into the model that way, or is there a different way to deal with interactions?

Let me know if you need more information or clarity.

Thanks,
CJ

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Interactions in QTLs
parts:
The percent variance explained for the individual QTL will also include the interaction effect. And in any case, the overall percent variance explained seldom matches the sum of the individual terms, due to associations among the genotypes.

I don't understand your question, "Is it right to fit interactions into the model that way?"

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Interactions in QTLs
parts:
The profile LOD curves when you have an interaction in the model will also include the interaction term: comparing q1+q2+q1:q2 and q2 alone, or q1+q2+q1:q2 and q1 alone. The threshold to consider is not just the main effect threshold.

To see whether there's evidence for an additional QTL on a chromosome, use addqtl().

karl
